summary.intent: Make the version command surface a warning when a changeset contains an unknown or unresolved entry, instead of silently ignoring it, in both text and JSON output.
summary.outcome: Aggregation diagnostics are now surfaced from version.rs, with a test added in status_version_selector_tests.rs. A mutation check, a changeset and a CI run were done, and a PR was opened. The transcript shows only tool descriptions, not their results, so CI pass/fail is not confirmed.

repo: Unresolved-entry diagnostics are produced during aggregation in aggregate.rs, which also handles the empty-changeset emission.
version.rs builds an aggregation and consumes its diagnostics, but they were not previously surfaced to the user.
The repo expects a changeset file for each PR and has a CI script that is run locally before opening one.
Work was done in a separate git worktree.
CLI tests in crates/callisto-cli/tests/status_version_selector_tests.rs cover both text and JSON output formats, and the format flag has to be passed correctly.

code.finding: Aggregation diagnostics are now passed through and reported from the version command.
A new test checks that the unknown-entry warning appears in the version output.

workflow: Reproduce the bug in both text and JSON output before changing code.
Run a mutation check, for example by reverting the fix to confirm the new test fails, to show the test actually guards the behavior.
Run CI locally and add a changeset before committing and opening the PR.

friction: The first version of the new test used the wrong format flag and had to be fixed.
Finding where aggregation diagnostics flow in version.rs took several rounds of searching and reading.
